limitations: Input and result output are text; saved workflow JSON is serialized in the result envelope. The envelope is bounded to 1 MiB.
Delegation limits are fixed in this slice. Legacy absent policy permits historical worker selection but never complete published-agent invocation.
Native Qwen/thread concurrency queues still apply. Awaited children require available harness capacity; delegated workflow root admission does not reserve Qwen process capacity.
Pending reservations reattach through explicit native replay/tool retry; no automatic boot queue or exactly-once effects are claimed.
P4.3 retains explicit abrupt nested/admission-window crash tests, recovery hardening and directly reopened-child parent provenance.
The workflow call remains queued while the core invocation is running; its agentInvocation metadata exposes the actual child state.
Docker uses stock Qwen and a deterministic model fixture, not corporate harness authorization.
verificationNotes: Real migrated SQLite verifies authority, key conflicts, per-root depth/outstanding/total budgets, expired native thread/workflow dispatch, lost admission replies and cancellation during delayed admission.
Native workflow scheduler tests cover delegated admission at ordinary root capacity and maintenance fences.
The plugin lifecycle facade forwards and fences all new internal methods, including stop callback generations.
The Qwen Unix-socket profile parser accepts delegation and workflow metadata while rejecting malformed/duplicate/unknown policy fields.
Default bundled Chromium also crashed on about:blank on this host; production browser checks use installed Chrome.

The token-revocation fixture preserves existing workflow/automation 401 assertions after restart, then performs fresh certificate authorization only for the new two-owner composition checks and logs out again.
